facts.label: Credit analysis by dimension
facts.text: Leverage rose because EBITDA fell, not because debt grew. Total debt at carrying value was USD 3,194.274 million at the 2025 year end and USD 3,186.368 million at the 2026 year end, while Total Reported EBITDA fell 12.72% to USD 753.042 million as skier visits fell 13.4% in a record-low snowfall season. The composition of debt changed more than its size: the convertible notes were repaid in cash at maturity on 2026-01-02, funded by a delayed draw term loan and cash on hand, and USD 180.000 million was drawn on the revolver at the year end against nothing a year earlier. The consequence for creditors is that the same debt is now serviced by a smaller and more seasonal EBITDA base, which moves total debt to EBITDA from 3.70x to 4.23x. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 112, 114, 132, 156, 162; 10-K_2025-07-31_mtn-20250731.htm.jsonl, page 95; calculation C30; calculation C25; Source readiness (CP-0)

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Earnings rest on one weather-dependent segment with high operating leverage, so a poor season reaches creditors' cash flow quickly. The Mountain segment was 88.20% of net revenue and 96.85% of Total Reported EBITDA in fiscal 2026, and Resort Reported EBITDA fell 11.66% on a 4.45% fall in Resort revenue, a decremental margin of 74.65%, even after USD 45 million of efficiency savings. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that fiscal 2026 was an extreme weather year and the issuer still held the fall in EBITDA to 12.72% on a 13.4% fall in skier visits, because effective ticket price rose 11.5%, passes were about 70% of lift revenue and costs flexed with USD 45 million of efficiency savings. The dividend alone was 1.28x free cash flow, so a cut would restore coverage; almost all debt matures in fiscal 2030 or later; the issuer reports compliance with every financial covenant and expects it for the next twelve months; and total leverage would return to 3.69x if EBITDA recovered to the fiscal 2025 level with debt unchanged. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: A second season with weak western snowfall is the realistic downside, because fiscal 2026 showed how it works. Poor early-season conditions cut visits and paid lift revenue, ancillary revenue falls with them, pass renewals for the following season weaken as they already have for 2026/2027, and the fixed cost base passes about three quarters of each lost revenue dollar to EBITDA. Repeating the fiscal 2026 change in EBITDA with everything else unchanged takes EBITDA 13.08% lower, total leverage to 4.87x and cash interest cover to 3.51x, and leaves dividends above free cash flow by an amount equal to 22.51% of liquidity, which the revolver and cash can fund for a year but which would take drawn revolver borrowings above their level at the 2026 year end. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 94, 115, 117, 119, 120; calculation C15; calculation C10

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Vail Resorts presents an adequate business profile supported by an owned network of 42 resorts, a pass model that brings cash in before the season and costs and capital spending that can be flexed, but credit quality is constrained by earnings concentrated in one weather-exposed segment, total leverage of 4.23x and cash interest cover of 4.04x, and payouts above free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears adequate for one weak season and weak for two, because free cash flow conversion has fallen to 32.93% of EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on leverage when the fiscal 2030 maturities approach, which enter the one-year window in 2029. The primary downside path is a second weak season with weak pass sales, and further analysis would require the executed debt agreements, the proxy statement and the pass sales outcome for 2026/2027. Top risk: a repeat of the fiscal 2026 earnings fall while dividends stay above free cash flow. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 112, 135, 167; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C06; calculation C23

## Request

Source readiness for Vail Resorts Inc (issuer mtn-812011), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: whether the four supplied filings can support the Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit work, and what is missing.
## Sources

| 10-Q_2026-01-31_mtn-20260131.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Vail Resorts, Inc. for the quarterly period ended January 31, 2026 (unaudited) | 2026-03-09 | 0429d8a825d64d833518a1cedbc48fb44ffcf0999cce431f9788c6f837aceffc | Six-month figures for deriving a first quarter, interim cash and revision lineage; the date is the signature date printed in the document |

No output of another module was supplied to this module.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The four filings support a source-based credit snapshot of Vail Resorts through the year ended 2026-07-31, but not a view of creditor protection, because no debt agreement was supplied and the filings name the covenants without printing their levels. Ratings, trading quotes, peer data and a first-quarter 2026 interim report are also absent, so those inputs stay unestablished rather than assumed.

Two points need care before any figure is used. The run settings name the third quarter of 2026 as the current period, yet the sources include the annual report for the year ended 2026-07-31, signed 2026-09-28, which is 51 days before the as-of date. The issuer also states that cash at the January and April 2026 quarter-ends was overstated by USD 38.8 million and USD 38.4 million because certificates of deposit were classified as cash. Both points are carried as open items, not reconciled here.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 172, 196; calculation C1

## Findings
### Bottom line

Reported leverage at Vail Resorts rose to 4.23x total debt to EBITDA at the 2026-07-31 year end from 3.70x a year earlier while debt was flat, and cash interest cover fell to 4.04x from 5.52x, leaving creditors less cushion after a record-low snowfall season.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 103; 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 112, 132, 133, 135; calculation C25; calculation C21; calculation C29

The ratios use carrying-value debt and the issuer's own Total Reported EBITDA with no add-backs. Net of cash the year-end ratio is 3.92x, and the effect of the dividend payable on 2026-10-27 is not established. At the April 2026 quarter-end the ratio was 4.03x on last-twelve-months EBITDA, using cash that the issuer later said was overstated, and no cash interest cover can be stated for that date.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 112, 172; 10-Q_2026-04-30_mtn-20260430.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C26; calculation C23; Source readiness (CP-0)

| Pro forma net debt after the dividend payable 2026-10-27 | Not Ready | The total dividend amount is not stated | Obtain the dividend total or the record-date share count |

| Discrete quarterly series | Ready with Limitations | Fourth quarter is fiscal year less nine months; investing cash flow carries the certificate of deposit distortion | Use annual cash flow for investing items |
### Credit analysis by dimension

Leverage rose because EBITDA fell, not because debt grew. Total debt at carrying value was USD 3,194.274 million at the 2025 year end and USD 3,186.368 million at the 2026 year end, while Total Reported EBITDA fell 12.72% to USD 753.042 million as skier visits fell 13.4% in a record-low snowfall season. The composition of debt changed more than its size: the convertible notes were repaid in cash at maturity on 2026-01-02, funded by a delayed draw term loan and cash on hand, and USD 180.000 million was drawn on the revolver at the year end against nothing a year earlier. The consequence for creditors is that the same debt is now serviced by a smaller and more seasonal EBITDA base, which moves total debt to EBITDA from 3.70x to 4.23x.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 112, 114, 132, 156, 162; 10-K_2025-07-31_mtn-20250731.htm.jsonl, page 95; calculation C30; calculation C25; Source readiness (CP-0)

Interest cover fell from 5.52x to 4.04x because cash interest paid rose 19.15% to USD 186.308 million while EBITDA fell. After capital expenditures of USD 231.625 million, EBITDA covered cash interest only 2.80x against 4.01x a year earlier, so a larger share of earnings now goes to lenders before any reinvestment. The amended credit agreement lowered the margin on the USD 1,423.125 million drawn under it, which should ease interest cost, but the filings print no figure for the saving.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 114, 133, 135, 158; calculation C31; calculation C29; calculation C40

Free cash flow after capital expenditures was USD 248.001 million in fiscal 2026 against USD 319.679 million in fiscal 2025, and it did not cover USD 317.131 million of dividends and USD 45.000 million of share repurchases, leaving a shortfall of USD 114.130 million met from cash and the revolver. Operating cash flow fell USD 75.244 million, and deferred revenue absorbed USD 39.564 million of cash against a USD 26.436 million inflow a year earlier. For creditors the dividend is the flexible use of cash, and the issuer states that it can respond to a weak season by managing capital expenditures, variable operating expense and the dividend.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 117, 135; calculation C17; calculation C34; calculation C32

Liquidity at the 2026 year end was USD 231.349 million of cash plus USD 513.300 million of undrawn revolver commitments, USD 744.649 million in total, against USD 83.908 million of debt due within one year, and no large maturity falls due before fiscal 2030, when USD 1,739.211 million matures. The cash balance sits near the seasonal low, because the issuer states that cash is lower at the end of the first and fourth fiscal quarters than at the end of the second and third. USD 37.112 million of short-term certificates of deposit sit outside the cash figure and would add to liquidity if counted.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 102, 112, 114, 132, 167; calculation C35

Customer prepayments are a float that funds operations before winter revenue arrives. Short-term deferred revenue, mostly pass products sold before the season, was USD 566.5 million at the 2026 year end against USD 602.1 million a year earlier, a decline of 5.91%, and pass sales for the 2026/2027 season through 2026-09-18 were down in units by approximately 12% and in dollars by approximately 6%. A second weak pass campaign would therefore reduce the cash available to service debt in fiscal 2027, and the Epic Coverage refund option adds to that exposure if another weak season follows.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 148, 150; calculation C44

Three data limits qualify every ratio. The issuer states that cash at both 2026 interim quarter-ends was overstated by USD 38.8 million and USD 38.4 million because certificates of deposit were classified as cash, so interim ratios use cash as reported and are labelled. The EBITDA measure is the issuer's own and excludes the USD 19.239 million fair-value charge on the Park City contingent consideration, which is a participating payment to the landlord, so a ratio that counted it would be higher. The issuer's net debt of USD 2,917.907 million also deducts USD 37.112 million of certificates of deposit that this module keeps outside cash.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 112, 172; 10-Q_2026-04-30_mtn-20260430.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C42; calculation C41; Source readiness (CP-0)

The strongest contrary evidence is that the weakness is weather-driven and the maturity profile is comfortable. The issuer reports compliance with all financial covenants at 2026-07-31 and expects compliance for the next twelve months, almost all of its debt falls due in fiscal 2030 or later, and fiscal 2026 was a record-low snowfall year. That view would win if pass sales stabilise and EBITDA returns toward its fiscal 2025 level, which would bring leverage back toward its fiscal 2025 level. The filings print no covenant levels, so the margin of safety under the covenants cannot be measured here.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 116, 120, 167; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Cash and cash equivalents at 2026-01-31 and 2026-04-30 are overstated according to the 2026 annual report, by USD 38.8 million and USD 38.4 million, and investing cash outflows for the six and nine months are understated by USD 37.1 million, because certificates of deposit were classified as cash. This restricts interim net debt, interim liquidity and any fourth-quarter cash flow built by subtraction, and the correction will appear only in the quarterly reports for periods ending 2027-01-31 and 2027-04-30. The action that would close it is a corrected interim balance sheet from the issuer. Severity: Medium.

- The issuer states no adjusted EBITDA and the filings print no covenant EBITDA, so every ratio rests on the issuer's own Total Reported EBITDA, and the adjusted ratio rows and the EBITDA bridge are not stated for any period. The action that would close it is the covenant compliance calculation from the executed credit agreement. Severity: Medium.

- Cash paid for interest is not printed in the quarterly cash flow statements, so last-twelve-months cash interest and interest cover at 2026-04-30 are not calculable. The action that would close it is the cash flow supplemental disclosure for the nine months. Severity: Medium.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-04-30_mtn-20260430.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 6

- No source states the legal rank or the security of the Vail Holdings Credit Agreement facilities or the Whistler facility, and the guarantors of the senior notes and the credit agreement are named only as certain domestic subsidiaries, so the debt stack is not stated, no cumulative leverage can be given and the structural position of each creditor class is not established. The action that would close it is the executed credit agreement, the indentures and subsidiary-level financial information. Severity: High.

- The total amount of the dividend payable on 2026-10-27 is not stated, so pro forma net debt and pro forma net leverage after it are not established. The action that would close it is the dividend total or the number of shares at the 2026-10-08 record date. Severity: Medium.

- The undrawn revolver commitments at 2024-07-31 are not stated in the sources, so the fiscal 2024 liquidity row has cash only. The action that would close it is the fiscal 2024 annual report. Severity: Low.
Basis: 10-K_2025-07-31_mtn-20250731.htm.jsonl, page 95

- The base on which the term loan amortizes at 5% of principal a year is not stated, and no principal schedule is stated for the finance leases, the NRP Loan or the EPR Secured Notes, so annual amortization is not supplied for those instruments. The action that would close it is the executed documents or the lease schedules. Severity: Low.

- The filings carry instrument-level carrying values only for the two senior notes, the EPR Secured Notes and the NRP Loan, so the carrying values of the other instruments are not separately disclosed; the net adjustment of -6,528 thousand on those instruments is derived from the aggregate premium and is not a printed figure. Severity: Low.

- Where the filings print a dash for a nil amount, the statement tables record Not supplied rather than zero, as the method requires; this affects short-term certificates of deposit in 2025, acquisitions in fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2025, certificate of deposit purchases and maturities, and note proceeds and repayments in years with none. Lines printed in only the annual or only the quarterly statements are likewise Not supplied for the other period. The action that would close it is the issuer confirming that dashes are nil. Severity: Low.

- No corporate or elimination line is printed in the segment note, because the issuer allocates corporate administrative expense to the segments, so the segment schedule has no corporate row and no segment sum is stated beyond the printed totals. Severity: Low.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 183

- The run settings name the third quarter of 2026 as the current period, while the latest filing is the annual report for the year ended 2026-07-31; both are shown and labelled and the period to treat as current is not resolved here. The action that would close it is the owner confirming the current period. Severity: Medium.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 196; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The first-quarter 2026 report is not supplied, so no first-quarter balance sheet exists in the statement tables and only the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 is built as a discrete quarter. The action that would close it is the quarterly report for the period ended 2025-10-31. Severity: Low.

spans.text: # Business & governance: Vail Resorts Inc (mtn-812011), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Business & governance for Vail Resorts Inc (issuer mtn-812011), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business and operating model, transactions and history, ownership and control, and governance and shareholder behaviour, from the four supplied filings and the source readiness output, with every limit stated.
## Sources

| 10-Q_2026-01-31_mtn-20260131.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Vail Resorts, Inc. for the quarterly period ended January 31, 2026 (unaudited) | 2026-03-09 | 0429d8a825d64d833518a1cedbc48fb44ffcf0999cce431f9788c6f837aceffc | Dividend declared 2026-03-05, the credit agreement amendment of 2026-02-09 as a subsequent event, the share count and an executive agreement exhibit; no interim cash is used; the date is the signature date printed in the document |

| 10-Q_2026-04-30_mtn-20260430.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Vail Resorts, Inc. for the quarterly period ended April 30, 2026 (unaudited) | 2026-06-08 | 2cb1e2366740b16bf429b8a197c1ee9af6d0cab60f11fb526dd196f76a8d00c9 | Dividend declared 2026-06-04, the share count and the interim cash figure used to size the later-corrected overstatement; the date is the signature date printed in the document |
Earlier module output supplied: Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 dbdd06f18acf3a080b6e3805987e77f9b8739c78b3f220face08df53e08d55c3.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Vail Resorts is a concentrated, weather-exposed ski operator whose advance pass sales bring cash in early but whose fixed costs and shareholder payouts leave creditors exposed in a poor snow season; sponsor and governance risk is Medium because no creditor-adverse action is documented.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 97, 99, 101, 103; 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 119, 135; calculation C02; calculation C07; calculation C16

The Mountain segment produced 96.85% of Total Reported EBITDA in fiscal 2026, and a 13.4% fall in skier visits cut Resort Reported EBITDA by 11.66% on a 4.45% fall in Resort revenue. Dividends were 2.15x net income attributable to Vail Resorts, and the supplied documents include no executed debt agreement and no proxy statement, so the legal strength of creditor protection is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 103, 133, 135, 183, 190; calculation C02; calculation C06; calculation C05; calculation C13; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

- Earnings rest on one weather-dependent segment with high operating leverage, so a poor season reaches creditors' cash flow quickly. The Mountain segment was 88.20% of net revenue and 96.85% of Total Reported EBITDA in fiscal 2026, and Resort Reported EBITDA fell 11.66% on a 4.45% fall in Resort revenue, a decremental margin of 74.65%, even after USD 45 million of efficiency savings. The filings describe a cost base with a significant fixed component, which is why Resort EBITDA fell more than twice as fast as Resort revenue.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 99, 101, 149, 183; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C07

- The pass programme steadies revenue but front-loads the cash cycle, and the first reading on the next season is weaker. Pass products were about 70% of lift revenue in fiscal 2026 against 65% a year earlier and pass revenue rose USD 38.8 million while paid lift revenue fell 17.5%; pass sales for 2026/2027 through 2026-09-18 were down about 12% in units and about 6% in dollars, so fiscal 2027 starts from less advance cash, and the Epic Coverage refund terms would cut pass revenue further if another season closes early.

- Operating rights rest on public-land permits, leases and concessions rather than freehold title, so enterprise value depends on renewals and fee terms. Forest Service permits run to 2029-12-31 for Breckenridge and 2031-12-01 for Vail Mountain with fees of 1.5% to 4.0% of adjusted gross revenue, the company says it is not aware of a refusal to renew an operating ski resort permit, and the Grand Teton concession moves from a flat fee of 8.01% to a tiered fee of 14% to 22% from 2027-01-01, subject to review by Congress; the sales base is not stated, but variable franchise fees for the park concessions were USD 6.7 million in fiscal 2026, which caps the annual step at about USD 5.01 million to USD 11.7 million, or 30.70% to 71.71% of fiscal 2026 Lodging Reported EBITDA.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 40, 41, 48, 152; calculation C23; calculation C24

- Structure puts debt in subsidiaries and limits the cash that can move up to the parent. The parent is a holding company, the bank borrower is a wholly owned subsidiary, the Whistler facility and the secured notes assumed with Peak Resorts restrict distributions, and noncontrolling interests equal 56.85% of total stockholders' equity, so claims and cash leakage exist below the parent that the supplied documents do not size.

- Shareholder payouts, not acquisitions, are now the main use of cash that competes with creditors, and they have outrun free cash flow. Dividends and repurchases were 1.52x free cash flow over fiscal 2024 to fiscal 2026 and dividends alone were 2.15x fiscal 2026 net income attributable to Vail Resorts, while equity attributable to Vail Resorts fell 43.34% and goodwill and intangibles exceed total stockholders' equity. Repurchases were cut to USD 45 million in fiscal 2026 from USD 270 million, which shows flexibility, but the quarterly dividend of USD 2.22 per share was held and the latest one is to be funded from available liquidity rather than cash on hand.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 94, 133, 135; 10-K_2025-07-31_mtn-20250731.htm.jsonl, page 86; calculation C16; calculation C13; calculation C18; calculation C19

- Overall, governance risk is Medium: the evidence supports no controlling-holder or creditor-adverse conclusion, but disclosure has been uneven and the information that would settle control is not supplied. The annual report is signed by a chief executive who is also chairperson, the company reports two nominations of five director candidates for the 2026 annual meeting, and two interim reports overstated cash by USD 38.8 million and USD 38.4 million because certificates of deposit were counted as cash; against that, the auditor gave unqualified opinions on the statements and internal control, the notes print no related-party transaction or management fee, and affiliates hold about 1.00% of shares on an indicative basis, so there is no disclosed sponsor to support or to extract from the issuer.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 84, 129, 172, 190, 197; 10-Q_2026-01-31_mtn-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C22; calculation C29; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Acquisition risk is low for now, but lease-type claims ahead of equity are large. The last acquisition was Crans-Montana in May 2024, paid in cash, and no acquisition payment followed in fiscal 2025 or fiscal 2026, while the Canyons lease obligation and the USD 97.8 million of Park City contingent consideration, which the auditor treated as a critical audit matter, are fixed and variable claims of the landlord that rank beside funded debt.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 116, 131, 135, 156, 166, 172, 173; calculation C25; calculation C26
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that the shortfall is weather-driven and the network is broad. The company operates 42 resorts across North America, Europe and Australia, Destination guests rose to 58% of destination-resort visits from 56%, pass revenue rose USD 38.8 million in fiscal 2026 even as paid lift revenue fell 17.5%, efficiency savings of USD 45 million cushioned EBITDA, repurchases were cut to USD 45 million, the auditor gave unqualified opinions, and no priming, exchange or other creditor-adverse action is documented.

The view would soften if pass sales for 2026/2027 recover toward the prior year, if payouts fall back inside free cash flow, and if the proxy statement and the executed debt agreements show no concentrated holder and tight restricted-payment limits. It would worsen if a second weak pass campaign, a dividend held above free cash flow, the loss or repricing of a permit or concession, or a contested board changes financial policy, in which case the governance level would move above Medium.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 94, 101, 120; calculation C16
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so the Medium governance level could move either way if it shows a concentrated holder, related-party dealings, board control rights or pay terms tied to payouts.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 190

- No executed credit agreement, indenture or subsidiary financial statements are supplied, so the holding-company finding cannot be sized: restricted-payment capacity, guarantor coverage and cash held outside the guarantor group are not established, and the dividend and repurchase findings describe willingness, not legal capacity.

- Nothing dated after 2026-09-28 is supplied although the as-of date is 2026-11-18, so the weak pass-sales reading may be stale and payment of the dividend due on 2026-10-27 is not confirmed, which could change both the pass programme and the payout findings.

- Resort-level results, pass revenue in dollars and the sales base of the Grand Teton concession are not disclosed, so concentration by resort cannot be quantified, the cost of the fee step-up is bounded but not stated, and the operating leverage finding rests on segment totals.

- Interim cash was overstated until the issuer's later account and no corrected interim statements are supplied, so the disclosure-quality part of the governance finding rests on the issuer's own description of the error and an uncorrected interim report remains in the record until 2027.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The company has grown by acquisition but has made no acquisition payment since the purchase of Crans-Montana on 2024-05-02 for CHF 97.2 million (USD 106.8 million), funded with cash on hand; the cash flow statements print no acquisition payments in fiscal 2025 or fiscal 2026. Earlier acquisitions built the network through the Canyons lease in 2013, Park City in 2014, Whistler Blackcomb in 2016, Peak Resorts in 2019, Seven Springs in 2021 and Andermatt-Sedrun in 2022; Peak Resorts, the Canyons lease and Andermatt-Sedrun left claims that remain outstanding, namely EPR Secured Notes of USD 114.162 million at 9.52% to 12.88%, a Canyons obligation of USD 380.533 million with contingent payments to the landlord, and an NRP Loan of USD 34.025 million.

New debt issues since 2024 were refinancings rather than growth funding. In May 2024 the company issued USD 600.0 million of 6.50% senior notes due 2032 at par to redeem USD 600.0 million of 6.25% notes due 2025, and in July 2025 it issued USD 500.0 million of 5.625% senior notes due 2030 at par; both are unsecured, guaranteed by certain domestic subsidiaries, redeemable from 2027, subject to a change of control offer at 101% and free of financial maintenance covenants. The 0.0% convertible notes of USD 525.0 million matured on 2026-01-02 and were repaid in cash from a USD 275.0 million delayed draw term loan drawn on 2025-12-26 and cash on hand. On 2026-02-09 the credit agreement was amended and restated with a new USD 1,275.0 million term loan, a maturity that falls to 2030-04-16 while the 2030 notes remain outstanding, and a lower margin, which the annual report prints as SOFR plus 1.50% in the debt note and SOFR plus 1.88% for new borrowings in the liquidity discussion.

Two items sit outside the debt table or beside it and matter to creditors. The Park City contingent consideration of USD 97.8 million is a liability that the auditor treated as a critical audit matter, and a new finance lease for the Canyons Parking Garage added a liability of USD 22.2 million at commencement. The Canadian Whistler facility was amended on 2025-09-24 to a 2030-09-24 maturity and a smaller size of C$250.0 million and was undrawn at 2026-07-31.

After the year end the Board approved a dividend of USD 2.22 per share on 2026-09-24, payable on 2026-10-27, the company entered net investment hedges on its Swiss operations in August 2026, and pass sales for 2026/2027 were reported below the prior year through 2026-09-18. None of these is in the fiscal 2026 figures, the total dividend is not stated, and no new debt issue after 2026-02-09 is stated in the supplied documents.

spans.text: # Fundamental credit: Vail Resorts Inc (mtn-812011), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Fundamental credit for Vail Resorts Inc (issuer mtn-812011), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the overall credit view, downside path and monitoring triggers built from the four supplied filings and the three earlier module outputs, with every limit stated.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-07-31_mtn-20250731.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K of Vail Resorts, Inc. for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2025 | 2025-09-29 | 55cdabd1a82ef88ab6cacd962e88866108993f34d707bcb6f2706c474539360f | Fiscal 2024 debt and Net Debt reconciliation and fiscal 2025 revolver availability for the comparisons; the date is the signature date printed in the document |

| 10-Q_2026-01-31_mtn-20260131.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Vail Resorts, Inc. for the quarterly period ended January 31, 2026 (unaudited) | 2026-03-09 | 0429d8a825d64d833518a1cedbc48fb44ffcf0999cce431f9788c6f837aceffc | Read for the February 2026 credit agreement amendment as a subsequent event; no interim figure is carried into this view; the date is the signature date printed in the document |

| 10-Q_2026-04-30_mtn-20260430.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Vail Resorts, Inc. for the quarterly period ended April 30, 2026 (unaudited) | 2026-06-08 | 2cb1e2366740b16bf429b8a197c1ee9af6d0cab60f11fb526dd196f76a8d00c9 | Read for the interim cash caution and the nine-month position; no interim figure is carried into this view; the date is the signature date printed in the document |
Earlier module output supplied: Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 dbdd06f18acf3a080b6e3805987e77f9b8739c78b3f220face08df53e08d55c3.
Earlier module output supplied: Financial foundation (CP-1), sha256 9467b1518a98f35322f5cdadc11e82fb9314311927eeaa8bb3a008f271b7fa02.
Earlier module output supplied: Business & governance (CP-1A), sha256 58149eb8d4e2884794ad0497c81701a89cdf5346155dae9781020220f51813a3.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Vail Resorts is an adequate but weakening credit: a weather-driven 12.72% fall in Total Reported EBITDA lifted total leverage to 4.23x from 3.70x with debt flat, and payouts above free cash flow leave less room for a second weak season.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 112, 132, 135; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C04; calculation C01; calculation C10

Creditors have time but not much cushion: only 7.08% of principal falls due before fiscal 2030, the issuer holds USD 231.3 million of cash and USD 513.3 million of undrawn revolver commitments, and debt due within a year is 11.27% of that liquidity, yet cash interest cover fell to 4.04x from 5.52x and the covenant levels are not printed, so headroom cannot be measured. The effect of the dividend payable on 2026-10-27 on cash and leverage is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 102, 114, 120, 132, 167; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C13; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C03
### Key findings

- Leverage rose because earnings fell, and the cash cost of the same debt is higher. Total debt was flat while Total Reported EBITDA fell 12.72% on a 4.26% fall in revenue, so total leverage moved to 4.23x from 3.70x and net leverage to 3.92x from 3.19x, and cash interest paid rose 19.15% as zero-coupon convertible notes were replaced by floating-rate bank debt, although the filings print no bridge of the increase. The effect of the dividend payable on 2026-10-27 on net leverage is not established.

Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 112, 114, 133, 135, 158, 161, 162; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C18; calculation C19

- Cash generation covers operations and capital expenditure but not the payout, and conversion is falling. Free cash flow fell 22.42% and equalled 32.93% of EBITDA against 37.05%, cash interest and capital expenditure absorbed 55.50% of EBITDA against 45.38%, and dividends alone were 1.28x free cash flow, so the payout drew on cash, which fell 47.46% in a year that also saw USD 525.0 million of convertible notes repaid, and USD 180.0 million was drawn on the revolver at the year end against none a year earlier. Lower cash taxes, down 56.74%, cushioned the year, and the issuer says it can respond to a weak season through capital expenditure, variable operating expense, real estate timing and the dividend. The effect of the dividend payable on 2026-10-27 on cash is not established.

Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 112, 114, 117, 135, 156; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C10; calculation C09; calculation C11

- Liquidity covers the next twelve months but sits at the seasonal low and has shrunk. Cash and undrawn revolver commitments were 35.93% lower than a year earlier, the Vail Holdings revolver has USD 337.4 million available after USD 180.0 million drawn and USD 82.6 million of letters of credit, the issuer says cash is lowest at the end of the first and fourth quarters, and availability under that facility depends on a leverage ratio whose level is not printed. USD 37.1 million of certificates of deposit sit outside cash. The effect of the dividend payable on 2026-10-27 on this liquidity is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 102, 112, 114, 120; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C11; calculation C21

- Maturities give time, but they cluster in fiscal 2030 and will be priced on leverage at that point. Only 7.08% of principal falls due before fiscal 2030 and 54.62% falls due in fiscal 2030, when the bank facilities, which mature 90 days before the 2030 senior notes, and those notes come due; the filings print two margins for the bank facilities, 1.50% and 1.88% over SOFR, without saying why, so the cost of that refinancing is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 114, 158, 159, 161, 167; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; calculation C22; calculation C23

- The business can absorb one bad season but not a run of them, because earnings sit in one weather-exposed activity and the next season starts weaker. The Mountain segment produced 96.85% of EBITDA, 74.65% of each lost revenue dollar reached EBITDA, and pass sales for 2026/2027 were down about 12% in units and about 6% in dollars through 2026-09-18, so a repeat of the fiscal 2026 change in EBITDA would take it 13.08% lower, total leverage to 4.87x and cash interest cover to 3.51x, an arithmetic sensitivity and not a forecast.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 149, 183; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C16; calculation C15

- Financial policy, not sponsor behaviour, is the governance issue: there is no controlling holder, but dividends were 1.28x free cash flow, equity attributable to Vail Resorts fell 43.34% and the covenant levels that would show how much the lenders allow are not printed, so the Medium governance level in Business & governance holds only while payouts follow earnings.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 94, 120, 133, 135; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C10; calculation C17

- Creditor rank and security are not established, so this view draws no recovery or priority conclusion: the filings print no legal rank or security for the bank facilities, the senior notes are unsecured and guaranteed by certain domestic subsidiaries, the EPR Secured Notes carry 9.52% to 12.88% and are secured on seven resorts, and the Whistler facility and Peak Resorts restrict distributions.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 82, 158, 160, 161, 163, 164; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that fiscal 2026 was an extreme weather year and the issuer still held the fall in EBITDA to 12.72% on a 13.4% fall in skier visits, because effective ticket price rose 11.5%, passes were about 70% of lift revenue and costs flexed with USD 45 million of efficiency savings. The dividend alone was 1.28x free cash flow, so a cut would restore coverage; almost all debt matures in fiscal 2030 or later; the issuer reports compliance with every financial covenant and expects it for the next twelve months; and total leverage would return to 3.69x if EBITDA recovered to the fiscal 2025 level with debt unchanged.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 99, 101, 103, 117, 120, 167; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C04; calculation C10; calculation C14

The view would improve if pass sales for 2026/2027 close near the prior year, if the dividend is reset inside free cash flow and if the executed debt agreements confirm covenant room. It would worsen if a second weak season repeats the fiscal 2026 change, which on the arithmetic above takes leverage to 4.87x and leaves dividends above free cash flow by an amount equal to 22.51% of liquidity, if revolver borrowings at the next year end exceed USD 180.0 million, or if lenders require an amendment before the 2030 maturities enter the one-year window in 2029.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 102, 156; calculation C15; calculation C23
### Limitations

- Covenant levels, the Adjusted EBITDA definition and the conditions of revolver availability are not printed, so headroom is not established and the liquidity and refinancing findings assume the revolver stays available; a tight covenant would turn the constrained view into an impaired one, and a loose one would ease it.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 120

- The downside sensitivity repeats the fiscal 2026 change mechanically and holds taxes, working capital and management action constant, so it shows direction and order of magnitude only and may overstate the damage if the dividend is cut or understate it if cash taxes rise.
Basis: calculation C15

- Earnings are the issuer's own Total Reported EBITDA with no adjusted measure, so leverage on the lenders' definition may differ in either direction and every ratio in this view is on a reported basis.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 112

- No agency rating, market price or peer data is supplied, so the view of market access rests on the issuer's own record of issuing notes at par in 2024 and 2025 and relative credit standing is not assessed.

- The filings print no bridge of the rise in interest, so the finding that zero-coupon notes were replaced by floating-rate bank debt is an inference from instrument terms and balances, and the cost of debt could rise or fall from here by other amounts.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 135, 158, 162; calculation C19
### Strengths and weaknesses

- Strength: the network is large and owned, which spreads weather risk across regions and countries. Vail Resorts operates 42 resorts, four of the ten most visited in the United States, with 17.9% of North American skier visits, and fiscal 2026 showed the benefit when eastern resorts held visitation better while the Rockies and Tahoe lost it, so one region failing does not stop the whole business from producing cash.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 13, 51, 104; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Strength: the pass model steadies revenue and brings cash in before the season. Pass products were about 70% of lift revenue, effective ticket price rose 11.5% while visits fell 13.4%, and deferred revenue of USD 566.5 million was collected before winter, so a weak season hits earnings through fixed costs more than through lost prepaid revenue.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 99, 103, 150; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Strength: costs and capital spending can be flexed. Labour is 41.49% of Mountain operating expense and hours fell with visits, USD 45 million of efficiency savings were earned, the calendar 2026 capital plan of USD 229.0 million to USD 234.0 million contains discretionary projects, and repurchases were cut to USD 45 million from USD 270 million, so management has levers that protect creditors in a weak year.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 115, 135, 183; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Strength: liquidity and the maturity profile leave time. The issuer holds USD 231.3 million of cash and USD 513.3 million of undrawn revolver commitments, only 7.08% of principal falls due before fiscal 2030 and the issuer reports covenant compliance, so there is no refinancing event in the next two years that the filings show.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 102, 120, 167; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C11; calculation C13

- Strength: the operating rights are hard to replicate. The issuer says no new destination ski resort of scale has been built in North America for over 45 years and its Forest Service permits run to 2029 and later with no refusal to renew known to it, which protects the asset base that debt rests on, although the claim is management's and renewal is not guaranteed.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 40, 41; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Weakness: earnings are concentrated and operationally geared. The Mountain segment produced 96.85% of EBITDA and 74.65% of each lost revenue dollar reached EBITDA in fiscal 2026, so a poor season converts quickly into lower coverage and leverage.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 149, 183; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C16

- Weakness: leverage and coverage have moved the wrong way for three years. Total leverage rose to 4.23x from 3.38x two years earlier, cash interest cover fell to 4.04x from 5.64x and free cash flow conversion fell from 45.71% to 32.93% of EBITDA, so each further earnings shock has less room to be absorbed.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 112, 135; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C06

- Weakness: shareholder payouts exceed free cash flow. Dividends were 1.28x free cash flow, equity attributable to Vail Resorts fell 43.34% and the latest dividend is to be funded from available liquidity, so cash returned to shareholders competes with debt service in a weak year.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 94, 133, 135; calculation C10; calculation C17

- Weakness: the next season starts weaker. Pass sales for 2026/2027 were down about 12% in units and about 6% in dollars through 2026-09-18, which lowers prepaid cash and pass revenue for fiscal 2027 unless the sales window closes better.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 101; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Weakness: creditor protection cannot be verified. Covenant levels, ranking, security and guarantor information are not printed, the EPR Secured Notes are secured and cost 9.52% to 12.88%, and distribution limits at Whistler and Peak Resorts mean cash is not freely available to the parent, so the true position of the senior notes is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 82, 120, 163, 164; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

### Source gate and status

The module runs with limitations. The audited statements, the debt note and maturity table, the segment note and the liquidity discussion are supplied, so every figure in this view rests on a printed source, but no executed debt agreement, proxy statement, agency rating, market price or peer data is supplied, so covenant headroom, creditor rank, relative value and market-implied views are not established here.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 120, 132, 158, 167, 183; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Business, ownership and revenue durability

Vail Resorts operates 42 destination mountain resorts and regional ski areas, and the Mountain segment produced 96.85% of Total Reported EBITDA in fiscal 2026 while Lodging added only a small share. Revenue comes mainly from lift tickets, which are about 58% of Mountain revenue, and passes are about 70% of lift revenue, so the business model gives visibility through advance sales but ties debt service to snowfall and to pass renewals.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 97, 99, 183; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C16

Ownership is dispersed with no controlling holder, the parent is a holding company whose bank borrower is a wholly owned subsidiary, and distribution limits at Whistler and Peak Resorts and noncontrolling interests below the parent reduce the cash that reaches creditors of the parent. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk Medium because no creditor-adverse action is documented, but the proxy statement that would show board independence and holders is not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 82, 133, 158; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Revenue is discretionary and weather-exposed rather than contractual: paid lift revenue fell 17.5% and ski school, dining and retail revenue fell between 6.5% and 10.3%, while pass revenue rose USD 38.8 million and Destination guests rose to 58% of destination-resort visits. The consequence for creditors is that a poor season hurts ancillary revenue first, and the Epic Coverage refund terms would reduce pass revenue if a season closes early.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 53, 98, 103, 104; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Cost structure, margin resilience and cash conversion

Costs have a significant fixed component, so margins fall faster than revenue: EBITDA margin was 26.53% against 29.10% and 74.65% of each lost revenue dollar reached EBITDA. Margins can be defended partly, because labour hours flexed with visits and USD 45 million of efficiency savings were earned, but a second poor season would find fewer easy savings, since the two-year programme that delivered them has been executed and the next phase is described but not quantified.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 99, 101, 104, 183; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C04; calculation C16

Cash conversion is the weakest part of the profile: free cash flow equalled 32.93% of EBITDA against 37.05% a year earlier and 45.71% two years earlier, because cash interest and capital expenditure now absorb 55.50% of EBITDA. Capital expenditure barely moved, at USD 231.625 million against USD 235.191 million, and the earnings left after cash interest, capital expenditure and cash taxes were below the dividend by USD 51.960 million before working capital, so the payout is the variable that decides whether creditors see deleveraging.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 112, 135; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C08
### Market forces and external factors

Competition comes from multi-resort passes sold by rivals and from other destinations, and the weaker 2026/2027 pass sales show that price and value are contested; entry into destination skiing is difficult, which the issuer says has produced no new destination resort of scale in North America for over 45 years, so the competitive pressure falls on price and mix rather than on new capacity. Labour and employee housing are the main supplier pressures, which is why the cost of staffing is a margin risk. The effect for creditors is a ceiling on pricing power and a floor on costs.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 19, 21, 101; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Regulation and macro conditions matter through four channels: permits and concessions that set the right to operate and the fee paid, discretionary consumer spending that follows employment and inflation, interest rates on the variable-rate share of debt after a 25 bp increase following the September 2026 meeting, and currency effects on the Canadian, Australian and Swiss earnings. Of these, weather and rates move credit metrics directly, while technology and social trends are not a primary credit driver on the filings supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 40, 41, 48, 50, 127; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position are strong, supported by 42 resorts and 17.9% of North American visits. Competitive advantage and business diversification are average, because the pass ecosystem lifts yield but 96.85% of EBITDA comes from one weather-exposed segment. Cost and capex flexibility and margin stability are average, with real levers but a high decremental margin. Free cash flow stability is weak, with conversion down for two years and payouts above it. Ability to refinance is average, with notes issued at par in 2024 and 2025 and the bank facilities extended in February 2026 but 54.62% of principal falling due in fiscal 2030. Liquidity is average, adequate for twelve months but at the seasonal low and 35.93% lower than a year earlier, and financial policy and governance are average and trending weaker. The effect of the dividend payable on 2026-10-27 on this liquidity is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 112, 135, 158, 160, 161; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C06; calculation C13; calculation C11

The trend is a gradual weakening: total leverage rose from 3.38x to 3.70x to 4.23x, cash interest cover fell from 5.64x to 5.52x to 4.04x and free cash flow fell for two years. The main supports are the pass model, the flexible dividend and the distant maturities; the main constraints are the concentration of earnings, the payout and the absence of verifiable covenant room; and the missing data are the executed debt agreements, the proxy statement and any rating or peer evidence.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 112, 135; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C03
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the weaker 2026/2027 pass sales and lower prepaid cash are the first headwind, partly offset by a full year of efficiency savings, effective ticket price that rose 11.5%, a capital plan with discretionary projects and Swiss growth capital of USD 12.0 million; variable-rate debt of about USD 1.5 billion means each 100 bp costs USD 14.7 million a year, and the 25 bp rise after the September 2026 meeting adds to that cost. Over three to five years the cluster of maturities in fiscal 2030, permit expiries from 2029, the step-up in the Grand Teton fee from 2027 and climate variability are the headwinds, while pricing, pass mix and digital engagement are the tailwinds the issuer cites.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 48, 50, 101, 103, 115, 127, 167; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C20; calculation C23
### Downside scenario

A second season with weak western snowfall is the realistic downside, because fiscal 2026 showed how it works. Poor early-season conditions cut visits and paid lift revenue, ancillary revenue falls with them, pass renewals for the following season weaken as they already have for 2026/2027, and the fixed cost base passes about three quarters of each lost revenue dollar to EBITDA. Repeating the fiscal 2026 change in EBITDA with everything else unchanged takes EBITDA 13.08% lower, total leverage to 4.87x and cash interest cover to 3.51x, and leaves dividends above free cash flow by an amount equal to 22.51% of liquidity, which the revolver and cash can fund for a year but which would take drawn revolver borrowings above their level at the 2026 year end.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 112, 135, 183; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C15; calculation C11

Management levers are real: a dividend cut of 52.85% would close the shortfall, repurchases can stay suspended, capital spending has discretionary projects and cash taxes would fall with earnings. Resilience therefore appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity event within twelve months, but not to avoid a further rise in leverage unless the dividend is reset, and the covenant level that would bound the revolver is not printed, so the point at which lenders would require action is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 94, 115, 117, 119, 120; calculation C15; calculation C10
### Overall credit view

Overall, Vail Resorts presents an adequate business profile supported by an owned network of 42 resorts, a pass model that brings cash in before the season and costs and capital spending that can be flexed, but credit quality is constrained by earnings concentrated in one weather-exposed segment, total leverage of 4.23x and cash interest cover of 4.04x, and payouts above free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears adequate for one weak season and weak for two, because free cash flow conversion has fallen to 32.93% of EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on leverage when the fiscal 2030 maturities approach, which enter the one-year window in 2029. The primary downside path is a second weak season with weak pass sales, and further analysis would require the executed debt agreements, the proxy statement and the pass sales outcome for 2026/2027. Top risk: a repeat of the fiscal 2026 earnings fall while dividends stay above free cash flow.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 112, 135, 167; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C06; calculation C23

## Gaps

- Covenant levels, the Adjusted EBITDA definition and the conditions of revolver availability are not printed, so headroom, the point at which lenders could act and the availability of the revolver in a downside are not established. The action that would close it is the executed credit agreements and the latest compliance certificate. Severity: High.

- The legal rank and security of the bank facilities and the guarantor scope are not printed, so creditor rank and recovery are not assessed in this view. The action that would close it is the executed documents and guarantor financial information. Severity: High.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 158, 160, 162; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- The final outcome of the 2026/2027 pass sales campaign is not supplied, so the weakness reported to 2026-09-18 may narrow or widen. The action that would close it is a pass sales update after the campaign. Severity: Medium.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 101

- The margin on the bank facilities is printed as SOFR plus 1.50% in the debt note and as SOFR plus 1.88% for new borrowings in the liquidity discussion, so the interest saving from the February 2026 amendment cannot be stated and the earlier statement in Financial foundation that the lower margin should ease interest cost holds only at the lower figure. The action that would close it is the pricing grid or the latest compliance certificate. Severity: Medium.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 114, 159; calculation C22

- The effect of the dividend payable on 2026-10-27 on cash, net debt and net leverage is not established because the total dividend is not stated. The action that would close it is the dividend total or the share count at the record date. Severity: Medium.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 94, 119; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- No agency rating, market price or peer data is supplied, so relative credit standing and market access are not assessed. The action that would close it is dated ratings, quotes and a peer set. Severity: Low.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- The filings print no bridge of the increase in interest between zero-coupon notes being replaced by bank debt, higher revolver use and other items. The action that would close it is the issuer's interest expense detail by instrument. Severity: Low.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 133, 135, 152; calculation C18; calculation C19

- The run settings name the third quarter of 2026 as the current period while the latest filing is the annual report for the year ended 2026-07-31; both are shown and labelled and the period to treat as current is not resolved here. The action that would close it is the owner confirming the current period. Severity: Medium.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_mtn-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 1; Source readiness (CP-0)
